acceptanceCriteria: `prove --attest-cem-v2` produces a DSSE envelope whose subjects include every artifact; verification refuses an artifact or --target that is not a subject.
Test: swapping one receipt file for another valid receipt under the same path with a re-signed map and the old envelope is refused.
All 54 public stable cases give identical verdictSha256 on native and portable consumers; a case with drift records out of order changes the digest.
cem-stable-v1.md and decisions 0354/0365 are amended in the same change.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Proposed CEM-V1-065 and CEM-V1-066. New predicate URI per FPK-V0-033; subjects are the stable map and every artifacts[] entry; predicate adds target {gitCommit, gitTree} beside base and patch. CEMStatementV1 and cem anchor call wire.ParseMap, which refuses cem/1.0 (CEM-V1-018); ParseMap routes the stable spec to ParseStable for attestation and anchoring. The verification result splits `verdict` from `environment` (runtime.goVersion, repository envelope) and publishes verdictSha256 over canonical verdict; later re-verification appends a record keyed by (mapSha256, target). Kill criterion K6: native and portable verdictSha256 differ on any public case.
title: cem/1.0 P1: `cem/v2` in-toto statement over map, artifacts and target; stable routing in attest/anchor; verdict/environment split with `verdictSha256`
